title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: SMEs struggling with AI implementation
sections.summary: Industry discussions report many SMEs struggle with AI implementation, especially workforce training and clear pathways, risking wider capability gaps without structured education and training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Yet, recent industry discussions reported in The Straits Times highlight that many small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are struggling with AI implementation, particularly in workforce training and identifying clear pathways forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This underscores a critical point, that technological progress, if unsupported by structured education and training strategies, risks widening capability gaps rather than closing them.

sections.label: Structured enrichment pathways for students
sections.summary: Students with strong aptitude should access structured enrichment pathways, and countries like Finland and South Korea have implemented nationally structured AI curricula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Students with strong aptitude should have access to structured enrichment pathways – advanced computing modules with AI components, collaboration with AI Singapore on student projects, supervised industry mentorships and national AI challenge competitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Now, Sir, I understand that countries, such as Finland and South Korea, have implemented nationally structured AI curricula that integrate technical skills with ethics and civic awareness from an early age.

sections.label: Tiered professional development for teachers
sections.summary: Teachers need proficiency in AI technologies, responsible embedding into lessons and assessments, and MOE is urged to implement tiered professional development programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They need proficiency not only in AI technologies but also in embedding them – how to embed them responsibly into lessons – designing assessments that measure critical thinking and supporting holistic development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I urge MOE to implement tiered professional development programmes for teachers.

sections.label: Supporting neurodiverse students with AI
sections.summary: Students with neurodiverse profiles, learning differences or disabilities must be supported, and adaptive learning systems can personalise content to pace, proficiency and cognitive profile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As we advance AI literacy, we must support students with neurodiverse profiles, learning differences or disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Adaptive learning systems can personalise content to a student's pace, proficiency and cognitive profile, providing targeted support to address gaps and reinforce strengths.

sections.label: Using AI to address class sizes
sections.summary: AI could creatively address class sizes, with the end goal of enhancing and improving the teacher-student ratio rather than simply reducing class numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Let us explore how we can perhaps use AI in a way that would be able to address the issue of class sizes in a creative manner, such that the end goal is not simply reducing the class size to smaller numbers in a class but enhancing and improving the teacher-student ratio.

sections.label: Dedicated AI CET centre
sections.summary: The Government could establish a dedicated CET centre for AI and data literacy for adult learners, offering modular programmes from foundational literacy to advanced applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government could consider establishing a dedicated CET centre focused on AI and data literacy for adult learners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A dedicated AI CET centre could offer modular programmes ranging from foundational literacy to advanced applications in responsible AI governance, sector-specific problem solving and workplace integration.

sections.label: AI education ecosystem call
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE, the Government and stakeholders to keep building a cohesive AI education ecosystem, calling this a pivotal moment for Singapore's education system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I urge MOE, the Government and other stakeholders to continue building a cohesive AI education ecosystem, one that nurtures curiosity, equips students for the future and ensures Singaporeans remain leaders and innovators in an increasingly digital, AI-augmented world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: This decision marks a pivotal moment in the evolution of Singapore's education system.

sections.label: Inclusive gifted education model shift
sections.summary: The new model keeps higher-ability pupils in their schools for after-school enrichment modules, reflecting a shift that excellence and inclusivity need not be mutually exclusive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: The new model, in which higher-ability pupils remain in their schools while attending after-school enrichment modules, reflects a broader shift in our educational philosophy, that excellence and inclusivity need not be mutually exclusive concepts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: Unlike the Secondary School-Based Gifted Education (SBGE) model, which is concentrated in "branded" elite schools and mirrors many clustering tendencies of the old GEP, the revamped primary-level programme allows us to reimagine excellence in a more inclusive and socially integrated way.

sections.label: After-school enrichment modules purpose
sections.summary: The modules should stretch brightest learners, broaden perspectives and reinforce social cohesion, not act as accelerated tuition or give PSLE advantage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: It gives us the opportunity to stretch our brightest learners, broaden their perspectives and reinforce social cohesion, cultivating students who are academically capable and socially grounded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: These after-school modules should not function as accelerated tuition, teaching more of the same content at a faster pace or providing direct advantage for the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE).

sections.label: Neighbourhood school enrichment approach
sections.summary: Situating enrichment in neighbourhood schools and broadening learning beyond examinations can combine academic excellence with inclusivity and social cohesion; it will be discontinued in its current form from 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: By situating enrichment within neighbourhood schools, broadening the scope of learning beyond examinations and nurturing pathways for high-potential students, we can combine academic excellence with inclusivity and social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: From 2027, it will be discontinued in its current form.

sections.label: Gifted students' socio-emotional study
sections.summary: A 2024 NIE study found gifted secondary students' academic environments produced lowered self-esteem, heightened stress and increased effort despite outward success, and the speaker asks how expertise will be scaled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A National Institute of Education (NIE) study in 2024 of intellectually gifted secondary students in Singapore schools found that their academic environments often produced a socio-emotional state of lowered self-esteem, heightened stress and increased effort, despite outward success.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How will this expertise be scaled across the system?

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will MOE adopt more child-led approaches, given that higher-ability learners can be self-directed?

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will MOE encourage more peer learning, so high-ability learners shift from a competitive mindset to a collaborative one?

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And how will schools safeguard students' psychosocial development and self-actualisation in a high-pressure environment?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As of 2024, classrooms averaged 34 pupils at the primary level and 33 in secondary schools.

sections.label: Teachers' weekly working hours
sections.summary: Teachers spend more than 47 hours a week working, six hours more than their OECD counterparts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our teachers spend more than 47 hours a week working, six hours more than their Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) counterparts.

sections.label: Teacher recruitment and Allied Educators
sections.summary: Singapore will raise teacher recruitment from 700 to 1,000 annually, while Allied Educators in teaching and learning would be scaled back.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Disappointingly, however, the news that Singapore will increase teacher recruitment from 700 to 1,000 annually was followed by a sucker punch.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Allied Educators in teaching and learning would be scaled back.

sections.label: Class sizes and teaching assistants
sections.summary: The Workers' Party calls to cap class sizes closer to the OECD average of 21, or add Allied Educators or Teaching Assistants to every classroom.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Redirecting the workload of teachers away from non-teaching tasks can only improve educational delivery.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I, therefore, reiterate the Workers' Party call to cap class sizes closer to the OECD average, which is currently at 21, especially at the primary level; failing which to complement every classroom with teaching and learning Allied Educators or Teaching Assistants that will serve the students and ensure that they succeed in the classroom of tomorrow.

sections.label: Household spending on private tuition
sections.summary: In 2023, households spent $1.8 billion on private tuition, with the top 20% spending over four times the bottom 20%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2023, households spent $1.8 billion on private tuition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The top 20% spent more than four times what the bottom 20% did.

sections.label: DSA admissions rise
sections.summary: DSA admissions rose from about 3,500 in 2019 to about 4,400 in 2023, around 11% of the cohort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: DSA was designed to broaden definitions of success and its intention is right.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But admissions rose from about 3,500 in 2019 to about 4,400 in 2023, around 11% of the cohort.

sections.label: Voluntary 10-year through-train pilot
sections.summary: MOE should consider a safeguarded, voluntary 10-year through-train pilot from Primary 1 to Secondary 4 with aligned standards and flexible class sizes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MOE should consider a carefully safeguarded, voluntary 10-year through-train pilot from Primary 1 to Secondary 4.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Under such a pilot, standards remain aligned with national expectations, students graduate with recognised qualifications such as the GCE, mobility and transfer options are preserved, and subject-based banding can start at an earlier age and deploy teachers according to the needs of the students using a “flexible class size” model instead of a “universal small class size” model.

sections.label: Optional PSLE and through-train pathway
sections.summary: The WP proposes making PSLE optional, with academically inclined students sitting it and others having a default through-train pathway to a partner secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The WP has proposed making the PSLE optional.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Students who are academically inclined can choose to sit the exam and compete for a select number of academically specialised secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Every other student should have a default through-train pathway to a partner secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should have an education system where the default is that every child passes through compulsory education without a high stakes written exam determining their trajectory at age 12.

sections.label: Removing secondary school affiliation advantages
sections.summary: The passage proposes removing secondary school affiliation advantages so all students compete on a fair footing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One practical step could be removing the secondary school affiliation advantages, so all students compete on a fair footing.

sections.label: National school start times standard
sections.summary: The passage calls for MOE to set a national 8.30 am start time standard and an integrated primary school day, citing sleep research.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us centre the child – and match or sort each one to a school where their unique potential can flourish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I am calling for MOE to set a national standard to synchronise school start times to 8.30 am for primary, secondary schools and junior colleges, alongside an integrated school day specifically for primary school levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The 2024 Singapore Youth epidemiology and resilience study shows nearly 85% of secondary school students feeling unrested, while Duke NUS research indicates they average only six and a half hours of sleep, well below the recommended eight to 10 hours.

sections.label: 8.30 am start and integrated school day
sections.summary: The passage proposes an 8.30 am to 3.30 pm integrated primary school day and a clear national standard instead of school autonomy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While MOE has brought forward personal learning device default sleep modes to 10.30 pm, we must also address wake times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Shifting to 8.30 am ensures students do not start their day exhausted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I propose an integrated school day for primary school starting at 8.30 am and ending at 3.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Rather than relying on school level autonomy, we need a clear national standard.

sections.label: Temperature increase cuts learning
sections.summary: The passage states each degree of temperature increase cuts learning by 1% to 2%, hitting lower-income students hardest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Research shows that each temperature degree of temperature increase cuts learning by 1% to 2%, hitting lower-income students hardest.

sections.label: Cognitive performance in fan-ventilated classrooms
sections.summary: The passage cites an NUS study finding cognitive performance drops 9% in slightly warm and 18% in warm fan-ventilated classrooms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A National University of Singapore study in Building and Environment found cognitive performance in Singapore's fan ventilated classrooms drops 9% in slightly warm conditions and 18% in warm conditions.

sections.label: Capital cost of classroom cooling
sections.summary: The passage states capital cost is less than $100 million for all classrooms, under 1% of MOE's budget paid once.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Capital cost, less than $100 million for all classrooms, under 1% of the MOE's budget paid once.

sections.label: Classroom temperature and air-conditioning
sections.summary: Asks whether MOE will set indoor temperature standards for classrooms and commit to a timeline for phased mixed mode air-conditioning, starting with primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will MOE establish indoor temperature standards for classrooms?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And will MOE commit to a timeline for a phased programme – beginning with primary schools – to install mixed mode air-conditioning in all classrooms?

sections.label: Primary school PE duration
sections.summary: States primary schools provide two to 2.5 hours of PE weekly, which is insufficient for children needing at least 60 minutes of daily activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Primary schools provide two to 2.5 hours of PE weekly, but logistics can eat into this short duration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is insufficient to build a robust physical foundation in children, who need at least 60 minutes of moderate to rigorous physical activity daily.

sections.label: Increasing primary school PE time
sections.summary: Proposes raising minimum primary PE curriculum time to five hours weekly, with qualified coaches supplementing PE teachers to address manpower constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: PE is therefore not a break from learning but a critical investment in our collective strength.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose increasing the minimum PE curriculum time in primary schools to five hours per week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address manpower constraints, MOE could supplement PE teachers with qualified coaches from the National Registry of Coaches and the National Registry of Exercise Professionals.

sections.label: AI-ducation for personalised learning
sections.summary: States AI-ducation personalises learning, identifies gaps and guides teaching, letting students progress at their own pace and freeing teachers for mentorship.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: AI-ducation – the use of AI to personalise learning, identify gaps and guide teaching – can help students progress at their own pace while freeing teachers from repetitive tasks to focus on mentorship and meaningful learning.

sections.label: AI feedback and differentiated instruction
sections.summary: States AI can provide real-time feedback, identify misconceptions early and support differentiated instruction at scale.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: AI can provide real-time feedback, identify misconceptions early and support differentiated instruction at scale.

sections.label: AI-enabled formative assessments
sections.summary: States AI-enabled formative assessments give real-time feedback, detect misconceptions early and adapt learning, reducing reliance on a single high-stakes checkpoint.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: AI-enabled formative assessments provide real-time feedback, detect misconceptions early and adapt learning as students' progress, reducing reliance on a single high-stakes checkpoint.

sections.label: AI formative assessment pilots
sections.summary: Asks whether MOE will pilot AI-enabled formative assessments at scale and whether such pilots could recalibrate timing and weight of high-stakes examinations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In that regard, will MOE pilot AI-enabled formative assessments at scale and could such pilots enable a recalibration of the timing and weight of high-stakes examinations?

sections.label: Expanding high-demand school capacity
sections.summary: Asks whether MOE could expand footprint and capacity of high-demand schools through additional campuses or increased intake in more locations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we are serious about reducing competition intensity, structural supply deserves consideration alongside the messaging.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, could MOE consider expanding the footprint and capacity of high-demand schools by establishing additional campuses or increasing the intake in more locations?

sections.label: DSA longitudinal data gap
sections.summary: States that without longitudinal data on students' progress, engagement, transition or early exit, DSA outcomes are difficult to assess.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Without longitudinal data on how these students progress through the DSA pathway, whether they remain engaged, transition successfully or exit early, it becomes difficult to assess both the intended and unintended outcomes of the DSA pathway.

sections.label: AI literacy beyond technical familiarity
sections.summary: States AI literacy must include questioning outputs, detecting bias, understanding limitations and exercising ethical judgement, not just technical familiarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: AI literacy must mean more than technical familiarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It must include the ability to question outputs, detect bias, understand limitations and exercise ethical judgement.

sections.label: Embedding AI literacy in education
sections.summary: States AI literacy must be embedded systematically and age appropriately across education, with teachers supported by guidelines and professional development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: AI literacy must therefore be embedded systematically and age appropriately across the education journey, with teachers supported through clear guidelines and professional development.

sections.label: AI literacy as national competency
sections.summary: States that as digital literacy became a baseline skill, AI literacy must now become a shared national competency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If digital literacy has become a baseline skill over the past two decades, AI literacy must now become a shared national competency.

sections.label: IHL curriculum for AI job market
sections.summary: The education system and IHLs must be agile in anticipating future skills demands in an AI-disrupted age, and the Ministry is asked how it will refresh curriculum and pedagogy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Our education system, especially our IHLs, must become more agile and proactive in anticipating future skills demands, especially in this AI disrupted age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: In light of this, how will the Ministry be ensuring that our IHLs refresh their curriculum and pedagogy to ensure that our students are ready for an AI-disrupted job market, with better chances of securing a good job?

sections.label: AI agent skills job postings
sections.summary: The Randstad Workmonitor 2026 Report states global job postings requiring AI agent skills surged by over 1500% in 2025 alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to Randstad Workmonitor 2026 Report, global job postings requiring AI agent skills surged by over 1500% in 2025 alone.

sections.label: Micro-credentials stacked into qualifications
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to set a timeline for cross-IHL micro-credential recognition, targets for fast-moving sectors, and annual progress reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Former Education Minister Chan articulated a vision in July 2024 of a living ecosystem, where micro-credentials from across our IHLs stacked into formal qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I ask the Ministry to set a concrete timeline for full-cross IHL recognition across universities, polytechnics and our ITEs so that adult learners can build towards a credible recognised qualification piece by piece with each step appropriately documented in the Careers and Skills Passport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But the pace of market demand is out running the pace of supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I ask the Ministry to set explicit targets for IHL micro-credential offerings in fast-moving sectors and to report progress against those targets annually so that we can hold ourselves accountable.

sections.label: Overseas stackable credentials recognition
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to extend SkillsFuture Credit eligibility and Careers and Skills Passport recognition to stackable credentials from reputable overseas universities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Massachusetts Institute of Technology's (MIT's) MicroMasters Programme on edX and Georgia Tech's Michael Masters in Analytics, which stacked directly towards their fully accredited and well-regarded online Master of Science and Analytics, are exactly the kind of high signals stackable credentials that carry global employer recognition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I ask the Minister to extend SkillsFuture Credit eligibility and Career in Skills Passport Recognition to such credentials from reputable overseas universities, not to replace our IHLs but to fill gaps while our local capacity develops.

sections.label: MIT study on AI essay writing
sections.summary: An MIT study found heavy reliance on AI tools for essay writing may cause long-term cognitive harm, weakened neural connectivity, poorer memory recall and reduced ownership of writing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, an MIT study published last year found that heavy reliance on AI tools for essay writing may lead to long-term cognitive harm as measured through brain scans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Students who repeatedly relied on AI had weakened neural connectivity, poorer memory recall and had a reduced sense of ownership over their own writing.

sections.label: Assessments without AI assistance
sections.summary: Instructors may use supervised assessments with restricted Internet access, and for take-home assignments more marks from vivas or oral examinations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where the objective is to assess independent thinking without AI assistance, instructors may use supervised assessments with restricted Internet access.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For take-home assignments, a larger proportion of marks come from vivas or oral examinations to evaluate the student's thinking process, even when AI tools are used.

sections.label: Temasek Polytechnic skills transcript
sections.summary: Temasek Polytechnic is pioneering a skills transcript for students graduating this year in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, Temasek Polytechnic is pioneering a skills transcript for students graduating this year.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and Workforce Singapore merger
sections.summary: The merger of SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore is significant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The merger of SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore is therefore significant.

sections.label: Longer-term employment outcomes matter
sections.summary: Longer-term wage growth, employment stability and quality of skills-job matching ultimately matter beyond enrolment and initial placement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Beyond enrolment and initial placement, what ultimately matters are longer-term wage growth, employment stability and the quality of skills-job matching.

sections.label: Preventing decision-making gridlocks
sections.summary: The new agency will report to both MOE and MOM, raising the question of how decision-making gridlocks can be prevented.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As the new agency will report to both MOE and MOM, how can decision-making gridlocks be prevented?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Taster Sessions proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes complementing existing SkillsFuture offerings with lower-cost or no-cost SkillsFuture Taster Sessions giving a flavour of industry or required skillsets.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, I propose complementing our existing SkillsFuture offerings with something simpler, lighter and decision-friendly.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I call this SkillsFuture "Taster Sessions", at lower costs or no cost. "Taster Session" itself gives a flavour of what industry is like or what skillsets you require.

sections.label: AI training accommodations for disabilities
sections.summary: Expanding TeSA to help non-tech workers gain AI capabilities signals AI is foundational, and training providers under national AI initiatives should incorporate reasonable accommodations for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Expanding the TeSA programme to help non-tech workers gain practical AI capabilities sends an important signal, that AI is no longer a niche skill, but a foundational one.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As we build these capabilities, we must ensure that inclusion keeps pace, especially for persons with disabilities, so that new divides are not created.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Training providers supported under the national AI initiatives should incorporate reasonable accommodations; such as screen-reader compatible materials, captioning or sign language interpretation where needed and accessible training venues.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify what requirements are in place to ensure such accommodations are consistently provided?

sections.label: McKinsey automation displacement research
sections.summary: McKinsey Global Institute research finds up to 30% of global work activities could be displaced by current technologies, with social and emotional skills least susceptible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: McKinsey Global Institute's automation research finds that up to 30% of work activities globally could be displaced by current technologies, with activities least susceptible to displacement being those requiring social and emotional intelligence, complex negotiation, empathetic judgment and creative collaboration.

sections.label: Singapore youth mental health data
sections.summary: The Institute of Mental Health study found one in three young Singaporeans aged 15 to 35 had a lifetime mental disorder, and PISA shows high test anxiety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Institute of Mental Health's National Study on Mental Health found that one in three young Singaporeans, aged 15 to 35, had experienced a mental disorder in their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: PISA data shows Singaporean students report among the highest levels of test anxiety of any participating country, with 86% of students reporting that they worry about poor grades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This is significantly above the OECD average of 66%.

sections.label: Protected hours for self-directed exploration
sections.summary: Two protected hours per week are for student-led, self-directed exploration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Two protected hours per week for student-led, self-directed exploration.

sections.label: Discovery Endowment Credits for Singaporeans
sections.summary: Discovery Endowment Credits give Singaporeans aged 15 to 25 opportunities for non-academic self-directed exploration, with a tiered structure considered for disadvantaged households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Discovery Endowment Credits will give for Singaporeans aged 15 to 25 more opportunities to discover themselves, a sense of awareness, self-management and develop maturity that is essential for long-term development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: These credits can be used for non-academic self-directed exploration, regional internships, acquire niche skills, independent project materials, or even get social enterprise grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: A tiered credit structure can be considered to help disadvantaged households address the documented reality where exploratory experiences are distributed unequally across income brackets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In the long term, this will potentially reduce the fiscal drag caused by mid-career burnout and career mismatch and its effects on absenteeism, healthcare utilisation and loss in productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Singapore's next phase of development requires citizens who can operate across the full cognitive and affective spectrum, who can think divergently as well as convergently, lead with empathy as well as analyse and navigate uncertainty with both intellectual rigour and emotional resilience.

sections.label: Oversubscribed ITE and polytechnic courses
sections.summary: A Woodgrove MP asks whether the Ministry can share occupancy or utilisation rates for ITEs, polytechnics and their part-time courses, citing disappointed qualified residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: From feedback in my constituency in Woodgrove, during every ITE and Polytechnic application period, many qualified residents are disappointed when their preferred courses are oversubscribed, even when their results actually meet the cut-off.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share the current occupancy or utilisation rates for our ITEs, polytechnics, as well as their part-time courses?

sections.label: Reviewing education financing schemes
sections.summary: The speaker urges reviewing and broadening the CPF Education Loan Scheme and Tuition Fee Loan to cover vocational trades, the arts, AI and sustainability courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To make these pathways truly inclusive, education financing must keep pace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I urge for a review and broadening of the Central Provident Fund Education Loan Scheme and Tuition Fee Loan to cover a wider range of courses – vocational trades, the arts and innovative fields like AI and sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   To support the implementation of the SkillsFuture initiative, the People's Association (PA) has been offering SkillsFuture@PA courses at various Community Clubs (CCs) since 2016.

sections.label: SkillsFuture@PA programme expansion
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the SkillsFuture@PA programme can be further expanded to encourage more Singaporeans to use their SkillsFuture training credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To encourage more Singaporeans to utilise their SkillsFuture training credits, I hope that SkillsFuture@PA programme can be further expanded.

sections.label: ITE progression and workplace competencies
sections.summary: The speaker asks how MOE will make ITE progression routes more visible, give formal weight to workplace competencies, and consider a conditional university pathway.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, can the Minister share how MOE will make ITE progression routes to the Work-Study Diploma and beyond more visible to students and parents, including pathway maps by sector and stackable credentials with clear milestones and entry criteria?

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, can the Minister update how MOE will give greater formal weight to workplace proven competencies with assessments that are rigorous and recognised across employers?

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Third, will the Minister consider piloting a structured conditional university pathway for top performing ITE and work study learners anchored on sustained workplace achievement and continued upgrading without implying that university is the only outcome?

sections.label: National Adult Educator Registry rules
sections.summary: From April this year, adult educators teaching SkillsFuture-funded courses must be on the National Adult Educator Registry and renew registration every two years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho
sentences.text: From April this year, adult educators who teach SkillsFuture-funded courses must be on the National Adult Educator Registry and renew their registration every two years by clocking minimum practice hours as well as taking up continuing professional development.

sections.label: President's Award for Adult Educators
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry would consider a President's Award for Adult Educators, like the President's Award for Teachers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho
sentences.text: Just as the President’s Award for Teachers recognises outstanding teachers who inspire their students and peers through innovative teaching methods and a commitment to lifelong learning, would the Ministry consider a President’s Award for Adult Educators as well?

sections.label: School cut-off points for affiliated students
sections.summary: The speaker's research found that for one popular school in 2025, the non-affiliated cut-off point was 10 and the affiliated cut-off point was 20.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In my research, I found that for one popular school in 2025, non-affiliated cut-off point, the student from non-affiliated school was 10, and affiliated cut-off point is 20.

sections.label: AL score mark ranges
sections.summary: The passage states that AL 6 spans between 45 and 64 marks, and AL 5 spans 65 to 74 marks.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, AL 6 spans between 45 marks and 64 marks, and AL 5, 65 to 74 marks.

sections.label: Affiliation cut-off points review
sections.summary: MOE could cap the difference between affiliated and non-affiliated cut-off points, review AL band mark ranges, or remove affiliation cut-off points completely.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Perhaps MOE can consider either capping the maximum difference between affiliated and non-affiliated cut-off points to two to three points, together with a review with the mark range within each of the AL bands to accurately reflect students' readiness, or maybe to remove affiliation cut-off points completely.

sections.label: Protected spaces for non-alumni students
sections.summary: MOE could consider more protected spaces for non-alumni students in oversubscribed schools so primary school choice is not driven by networks or resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To remain inclusive, I wonder could MOE consider more protected spaces for non-alumni students in oversubscribed schools so that primary school choice is not driven by structural advantage from networks or resources.

sections.label: Career exposure for disadvantaged students
sections.summary: Students from less resourced or disadvantaged backgrounds benefit more from career discovery opportunities because they lack professional networks and informal internships.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For students from less resourced or disadvantaged background, such opportunities to discover their interest matters even more, because if you come from a family without strong professional networks, you cannot easily borrow career insights from your parents or friends or find informal internships through social connections, because what you can see is what you can imagine and what you can imagine shapes what you dare to pursue.

sections.label: Standardising career exposure across schools
sections.summary: Career exposure should be expanded and standardised across schools through internships, externships, learning journeys, workplace visits, shadowing days and career days, aligned with priority sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, to expand and better standardise access to career exposure across schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This includes internship, externship, where feasible, but also shorter and more scalable formats, such as our learning journeys, workplace visits, shadowing days and structured career day with real job content.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, MOE should also consider a better structuring these experiences in line with our priority sectors or industry, where Singapore is trying to build our capabilities.

sections.label: Priority for those who gain most
sections.summary: For such programmes, priority should be given to those who will gain the most.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, for such programmes, priority should be given to those who will gain the most.

sections.label: Support for student participation
sections.summary: Simpler sign-up, transportation support and a small allowance if needed should ensure participation does not depend on a student's financial or family situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, it should be simpler sign-up, transportation support and if there is a need, for a small allowance, so that participation does not depend on the student's financial or family situation.

sections.label: National School Mental Well-Being Charter
sections.summary: Proposes a National School Mental Well-Being Charter with resilience education baseline, annual measurement instrument, and defined counsellor and peer supporter standards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: These are not optional add-ons, but structured expectations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: I therefore propose a National School Mental Well-Being Charter.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: First, a national baseline for resilience education: a minimum annual allocation within Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) for mental health literacy and coping skills; defined developmental competencies at key stages; central vetting of external providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Singapore can adopt a nationally validated annual instrument measuring belonging, coping confidence and psychological safety, used for internal improvement, not public ranking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our Charter should define timelines for counsellor access, minimum training and supervision standards for peer supporters, structured referral pathways.

sections.label: MOE partnership with arts practitioners
sections.summary: Asks whether MOE will partner arts practitioners to address bullying and build socio-emotional competencies in schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
sentences.text: Second, will MOE partner arts practitioners to address bullying and build socio-emotional competencies in schools?

sections.label: SEN officers and primary programmes
sections.summary: States SEN officers rose from about 450 in 2017 to about 750 by 2024, and primary schools run structured programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: SEN officers have increased from about 450 in 2017 to about 750 by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Primary schools now run structured programmes, such as School-based Dyslexia Remediation, Circle of Friends peer support, and the TRANsition Support for InTegration (TRANSIT) initiative.

sections.label: SPED capacity and manpower strategy
sections.summary: States capacity rises from 8,300 in 2024 to 10,000 places by 2030 and calls for a deliberate manpower strategy and a future SPED school model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Capacity will increase from 8,300 in 2024, to 10,000 places by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: If we build new schools without enlarging the workforce, we create a tug-of-war.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: We need a deliberate manpower strategy: expand sponsored training pipelines for SPED educators and allied professionals, scale structured mid-career conversion pathways, allow for foreign manpower to supplement the workforce, deploy regional multidisciplinary teams serving classes of schools, pace spread staff competitively, educators, speech pathologies, therapies and coaches.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Beyond expansion, we must ask: what should a SPED school of the future look like?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: It should adopt a lifelong learning model integrating academic foundations with work readiness and vocational exposure, life skills for independent and dignified living, social-emotional growth and community participation and AI tools that actively address the rapidly changing living and working landscape.

sections.label: Students with SEN in Singapore
sections.summary: States the speaker's interest and reports about 36,000 students with SEN in 2023, with about 29,000 in mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I would like to state my interest in this matter as a psychologist, special educator and also an academic with practice experience and research interest in the needs of students with SEN.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It was reported in the 2024 Disability Trends Report that there were, as of 2023, about 36,000 students with SEN in Singapore schools.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of these, about 80% or close to 29,000 attend mainstream schools, which represents a rise from the 27,000 in 2022.

sections.label: Cohort-wide learning readiness baseline
sections.summary: States a short cohort-wide baseline of 30 to 45 minutes could provide objective data on learning readiness skills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
sentences.text: A short, cohort-wide baseline around 30 to 45 minutes could provide objective data on learning readiness skills such as attention regulation, working memory and impulse control.

sections.label: Support for Primary 1 cohort
sections.summary: Where a Primary 1 cohort has higher-than-usual support needs, temporary para-educator or co-teaching support could be deployed earlier, and class composition or size flexibility considered where support density is high.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
sentences.text: Where a Primary 1 cohort shows higher-than-usual support needs, temporary para-educator or co-teaching support could be deployed earlier rather than after prolonged escalation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
sentences.text: And where support density within a class is particularly high, flexibility in class composition or size should be considered.

sections.label: Mother tongue learning support
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOE will support parents to immerse young children at home and use digital platforms, and says assessments should reward practical use, not just exam results.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: Too often, it is seen as an exam to pass and a source of stress rather than a living language.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: I ask whether MOE will provide greater support for parents to immerse young children at home and leverage digital platforms to make learning engaging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: Assessments should reward practical use, not just exam results.

sections.label: Community bilingual language initiatives
sections.summary: The passage proposes catalytic micro grants for community-led bilingual initiatives, regular community language spaces, and parent enablement toolkits and nudges for mother tongue use at home.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
sentences.text: First, we can consider catalytic micro grants for community-led bilingual initiatives – small, simple and outcome-focused – to support storytelling sessions, reading circles, drama and inter-generational activities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
sentences.text: Second, we should support regular community language spaces, for example, in libraries, community clubs or neighbourhood nodes, so that language use becomes a routine, not just an occasional festival.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
sentences.text: Third, let us strengthen parent enablement with simple toolkits and nudges that help families use mother tongue at home in practical ways, at meals, during routines and in shared activities.

sections.label: Full SBB and admissions changes
sections.summary: The first Full SBB cohort sits the SEC examination in 2027 and progresses to post-secondary education the following year, with admissions streamlined into a single Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise in 2028, and students who did well in Mother Tongue at PSLE may take Higher Mother Tongue from Secondary 1.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The first cohort of students under Full SBB will be sitting for the Singapore-Cambridge Secondary Education Certificate (SEC) examination in 2027 and will progress to post-secondary education in the following year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This common examination gives us the opportunity to streamline several admissions exercises into a single Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise for admissions to junior colleges, Millennia Institute, polytechnics and the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) in the year 2028, which will improve students' user experience and decision making.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Another move we implemented this year is to allow students who did well in Mother Tongue at the Primary School Leaving Examinations (PSLE) to take up Higher 	Mother Tongue from Secondary 1, regardless of their overall PSLE score.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This will give around 2,500 more students the opportunity to pursue their passion for their 	Mother Tongue language.

sections.label: Average form class sizes
sections.summary: The average form class size for primary and secondary schools is 34 and 33 today, respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The average form class size for primary and secondary schools is 34 and 33 today, respectively.

sections.label: Teacher recruitment numbers
sections.summary: Teacher recruitment has ramped up from 700 the year previously to a current target of over 1,000 new teachers a year, and over 1,300 teachers were recruited last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: He took issue with the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) explanation that it is not easy to hire many more teachers and that quality may suffer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have already ramped up teacher recruitment significantly – from 700 the year previously, to a current target of over 1,000 new teachers a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And last year, we recruited over 1,300 teachers.

sections.label: Allied educators and admin support staff
sections.summary: Allied educators in priority areas doubled from about 800 to 1,600 over 10 years, and administrative support staff rose from around six to nine per school.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In fact, as I shared in November, we have doubled the number of allied educators in priority areas, such as counselling and special education needs across all schools, over the last 10 years, from about 800 to 1,600.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The number of administrative support staff in each school has also increased, from around six to around nine in the same period, to help teachers offload some of their administrative workload.

sections.label: Broadening school-based programme access
sections.summary: Access to school-based programmes will be broadened from around 7% of the cohort today to 10%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister had shared at the 2024 National Day Rally, we will broaden access to such school-based programmes, from around 7% of the cohort today to 10%.

sections.label: Centre-based modules and GEP identification
sections.summary: At least double the current GEP cohort can take centre-based modules, with 15 primary school centres and a one-stage Primary 3 identification exercise this August.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Compared to the current GEP cohort, at least double the number of students will be able to take these centre-based modules, which cater to students with strengths in both specific as well as multiple domains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As a start, there will be 15 centres hosted by primary schools across Singapore, such as Palm View Primary and Yew Tee Primary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The first batch of Primary 3 students will participate in a standardised one-stage identification exercise this August, instead of the current two-stage process.

sections.label: Financial assistance eligibility and amounts
sections.summary: From Academic Year 2026, income eligibility criteria and financial assistance amounts were raised to benefit 31,000 more Singaporean students from lower- to middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: From Academic Year 2026, we raised the income eligibility criteria and financial assistance amount for Singaporean students to benefit 31,000 more students from lower- to middle-income households.

sections.label: Expanding schools with additional resources
sections.summary: From 2026, more resources will go to schools, expanding schools with additional manpower and funding from 100 to 157.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: From this year 2026, we will devote even more resources to schools, expanding the number of schools with additional manpower and funding, from 100 to 157.

sections.label: SPED schools and SEN support
sections.summary: Work with SSAs will build more SPED schools and places amid rising demand, while continuing to support students with SEN in mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Through our collective efforts, we help students live independently; learn for life; participate meaningfully in the community; and sustain meaningful employment for those who can access work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will work with SSAs to build more SPED schools and provide more SPED school places amidst rising demand, while continuing to support students with SEN in our mainstream schools.

sections.label: Reducing emphasis on academic grades
sections.summary: Recent changes include Achievement Levels replacing PSLE T-scores, fewer junior college admission subjects, and a Best subject for polytechnic admission.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To reduce the over-emphasis on academic grades, we have, in recent years: replaced PSLE T-scores with broader Achievement Levels; reduced the number of subjects required for junior college admission from six to five from 2028; and allowed students to offer one "Best" subject at minimally G2 level – or Normal (Academic) level equivalent – for polytechnic admission from 2028.

sections.label: Reviewing exams and posting
sections.summary: Areas open to review include milestone exams, DSA enhancement, and secondary school posting, including through-train options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For example, we are prepared to review how we conduct milestone exams and how the difficulty of such examinations should be calibrated; how DSA can be enhanced to strengthen student development, selection and its accessibility, so that it continues to meet its objectives; and how we post students to secondary schools, including the viability of through-train options, as discussed and suggested by Ms Denise Phua, amongst other areas.

sections.label: PSLE paper question balance
sections.summary: Each PSLE paper has 85% easy and moderate questions and 15% challenging ones, with scaffolding support for challenging questions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As such, every PSLE paper has a carefully calibrated balance of questions to cater to students of different abilities – 85% are easy and moderate, with 15% challenging questions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For challenging questions, Members may like to know that students are provided with scaffolding support to help them apply the concepts and skills that they have learned in less familiar contexts.

sections.label: Water poured between X and Y
sections.summary: Ray poured one-fifth of X's water into Y, then Sarah poured all Y's water into X, overflowing 120 cm3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Ray poured one-fifth of the water from X into Y to fill it completely, and then, Sarah poured all the water from Y in X, and 120 cm3 of water overflowed from X.

sections.label: Comparing structured and unstructured questions
sections.summary: The next page's question is the same but structured into two parts worth two and three marks, versus five marks at once.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Turn over the sheet and compare this with the question on the next page.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is essentially the same question, but structured, meaning that the question has two parts: (a), two marks; and then, (b), three marks, versus the first question, that dives straight in, five marks at one go.

sections.label: Second question from 2022 PSLE
sections.summary: The second question on page two was a maths question from PSLE in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The difference between the two questions, on page one and page two, is clear; and the second question, on page two that you are looking at, was a maths question from PSLE back in 2022.

sections.label: Education Conversations consultation series
sections.summary: A series of Education Conversations will be started to engage and consult educators, parents, researchers, students and the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But no one has a monopoly on good ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: That is why, in continuation of our efforts from Forward Singapore, we will start a series of Education Conversations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We intend to engage and consult educators, parents, researchers, students and the community.

sections.label: Primary 1 Registration places
sections.summary: Places at Phase 2C for students with no prior school connections rose from 20 in 2014 to 40 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Over the years, we have also made changes to the Primary 1 Registration Framework to expand access for students with no prior connections to enter our primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We had reserved 20 places at Phase 2C in 2014, which is open to students regardless of whether they have prior connections to the school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This was further increased from 20 to 40 in 2022.

sections.label: AI preparation in schools
sections.summary: Schools and IHLs will equip students to harness AI through the four Learns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To prepare our workforce for an AI-transformed future, our schools and IHLs will equip our students to harness AI through the four "Learns".

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme was introduced in 2024 to lower mid-career workers' opportunity costs of training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2024, we introduced the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme to further lower their opportunity costs of training for mid-career workers.

sections.label: New SSG and WSG statutory board
sections.summary: SSG and WSG will be reorganised into a new Statutory Board overseen by MOM and MOE to support Singaporeans in bridging skills to jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: At Budget 2026, Prime Minister announced that SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) and Workforce Singapore (WSG) would be reorganised into a new Statutory Board, jointly overseen by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and MOE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The new agency will integrate SSG's training and skills development capabilities, and WSG's employment facilitation ecosystem to provide stronger end-to-end support for Singaporeans in bridging skills to jobs.

sections.label: Review of educator salaries
sections.summary: MOE is reviewing salaries of educators, including Allied Educators and MOE Kindergarten Educators, and will share more when ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MOE is reviewing the salaries of our educators, including our Allied Educators and MOE Kindergarten Educators and will share more when ready.

sections.label: Cohort benefit increase
sections.summary: Around 10% of the cohort will benefit, up from 7% today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: With this, around 10% of the cohort will benefit, up from 7% today.

sections.label: Schools receiving additional resources
sections.summary: Schools receiving these additional resources will increase from the current 100 to 157.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Schools receiving these additional resources will increase from the current 100 to 157.

sections.label: Bilingualism and Mother Tongue funding
sections.summary: Funding for the Mother Tongue Language Learning and Promotion Committees will increase over the next five years to strengthen bilingualism through a wider range of activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In an increasingly fragmented world, bilingualism allows us to serve as a bridge between the East and the West, while helping us stay rooted in our local culture and strengthen our identity as Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Therefore, we will increase funding for the Mother Tongue Language Learning and Promotion Committees over the next five years to strengthen bilingualism through a wider range of activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Syed Harun will share details on our efforts for special education and promotion of 	Mother Tongue languages later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Chairman, the collective efforts of Singaporeans have helped to support and strengthen our students' learning experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In the spirit of "we first", we will keep working together with Singaporeans to improve our education system and weave a stronger social fabric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This work is more critical and urgent this fast-changing and uncertain world.

sections.label: Forward Singapore education enhancement
sections.summary: Under the Forward Singapore agenda, MOE will continue to enhance the education system and schools to help every child reach their full potential and make the system more student centric.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Under the Forward Singapore agenda, MOE will continue to enhance our education system and schools to help every child reach their full potential and make our system more student centric.

sections.label: Recent education programme improvements
sections.summary: Recent improvements include extending the Reading Remediation Programme to Primary 5 and Learning Support for Mathematics to Primary 3 and 4, refreshing the Mother Tongue Support Programme, and implementing Full SBB in 2024 for secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Recent improvements include the extension of the Reading Remediation Programme to Primary 5, as well as the Learning Support for Mathematics programme to Primary 3 and 4.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: The Primary 3 and 4 Mother Tongue Support Programme will also be refreshed to better engage students and narrow learning gaps.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Full SBB was implemented in 2024 for secondary schools, as part of MOE's efforts to nurture the joy of learning and develop multiple pathways to cater to the different strengths and interest of our students so they can achieve their full potential.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Under Full SBB, we have done away with separate Express, Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) courses, and our students get to learn, grow and work together.

sections.label: Post-secondary admissions exercise update
sections.summary: The first Full SBB cohort will sit the SEC examination in 2027, and MOE will update its posting system from 2028 and implement a new Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: The first Full SBB cohort will be sitting for the SEC examination in 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: As students take more diverse subject combinations, MOE has also reviewed the admissions criteria for post-secondary pathways, as announced at MOE's Committee of Supply in previous years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We will update our posting system from 2028 and implement a new Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise (PSE).

sections.label: New PSE single admissions process

sections.label: MOE study on classroom heat
sections.summary: MOE has studied rising temperatures' impact on learning since 1989, using passive cooling, fans, cool paint, breathable uniforms and mixed mode cooling, and commissioned a 2020 study.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: MOE has been studying the impact of rising temperatures on learning, believe it or not, since 1989, when then-Member of Parliament Mr Chandra Das first asked if MOE would air-condition our classrooms, and the implementation timelines.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Over the years, we have been careful not to rush into air-conditioning as the technology was not as energy efficient.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Instead, we have relied on passive cooling solutions and we designed our schools for maximum natural ventilation and for classroom windows to be north-south facing to minimise heat transmission.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: As temperatures have continued to rise, and as technology evolved in recent years, we have added more, faster and quieter fans to all classrooms, coated school building exteriors with solar-reflective cool paint, and we adopted uniforms with moisture-wicking or breathable materials to combat heat and humidity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We have also implemented mixed mode cooling in school halls with a target temperature.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: That is why we commissioned the study in 2020, which Mr Tiong cited, precisely to determine how best to apply mixed-mode cooling to bring about optimal thermal comfort conditions including temperatures in classrooms, while balancing other considerations such as long-term heat resilience and acclimatisation, energy consumption and impact on the environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I heard that the Minister said that he will consider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I was just wondering, is this kind of a "yes", "no" or "maybe" response, because this has been spoken about for quite a long time?

sections.label: Salary guidelines enhancements 2024 to 2026
sections.summary: Salary guidelines were reviewed and enhanced with salary enhancements from 2024 to 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: Since then we have reviewed and enhanced the salary guidelines with salary enhancements from 2024 to 2026.

sections.label: PSLE through-train Education Conversations
sections.summary: On PSLE and through-train, no suggestion will be off the table in the Education Conversations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On PSLE and through-train, as I said, in coming up with the Education Conversations, no suggestion will be off the table.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will not be closed off to any idea.

sections.label: MOE benchmarks fidelity consistency schools
sections.summary: A question asks whether MOE sets benchmarks to ensure fidelity and consistency of implementation across schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Does MOE set benchmarks to ensure fidelity and consistency of implementation across schools?

sections.label: Guidelines mental health counsellors support
sections.summary: MOE has guidelines on access to mental health needs, counsellors and support structures within schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: The first on benchmarks and fidelity, we do have certain guidelines with regard to how access to mental health needs, as well as the accessibility to counsellors, and the variety of support structures within the schools.

sections.label: Human instruction in classrooms
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether sustaining human instruction in primary and SPED classrooms remains paramount even in the age of AI.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Does the Minister agree that even in the age of AI, sustaining human instruction in our classrooms, especially in primary, but also SPED schools, remains paramount?

sections.label: Expanding Allied Educators sunsetted
sections.summary: Expanding Allied Educators and Teaching and Learning was sunsetted, announced about nine years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In (b), expanding Allied Educators, Teaching and Learning (T&L) has been sunsetted; we announced it quite a number of years ago, about nine years ago.

sections.label: Schools, SSAs and Primary 1 places
sections.summary: Schools work with SSAs through the ComLink Alliance Working Group and UPLIFT, and the Primary 1 admission framework is being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On schools working with SSAs, the answer is the ComLink Alliance Working Group as well as internally between the schools and HQ through UPLIFT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On Primary 1 places, if we were to, as I said, we are reviewing the Primary 1 admission framework to achieve the broad goal I mentioned earlier.

sections.label: MOE oversight and sports collaboration
sections.summary: MOE has oversight of framework development, and there is room for MOE to work more closely with the High Performance Sport Institute and national sports associations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have oversight from MOE for how they develop these frameworks, but the frameworks that they have for each campus is suitable for their needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: I also wonder whether my COS speech for MCCY has somehow been leaked, so the short answer to the Member's question is yes, there is room for MOE to work more closely together with the High Performance Sport Institute, and all the national sports associations, when it comes to nurturing that love and to be able to collaborate well, use some of the existing criteria and promotion frameworks to really do more for our student athletes.

sections.label: Community engagement details and measurements
sections.summary: Details of community engagement are still being developed, and Nee Soon South can discuss programmes with MOE; measurements are 7,200 cubic centimetres and 32 centimetres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: With regard to the details as to where in the different communities we will be engaging, I think it is still being developed in terms of the details, but certainly if Nee Soon South is keen to be able to engage MOE to develop programmes in keeping with the development of the MTLs, we can discuss that in further detail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For (a), it is 7,200 cubic centimetres; for (b), it is 32 centimetres.

sections.label: Primary level focus on fundamentals
sections.summary: At the primary level, the focus will remain firmly on fundamentals: literacy, numeracy, reasoning and character.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: Just to give a sense, at the primary level, the focus will remain firmly on fundamentals, like I mentioned, literacy, numeracy, reasoning and character.

sections.label: Mother Tongue teaching and school programmes
sections.summary: Feedback on Tamil teacher training curriculum review, and school-based and centre-based programmes for stretched students with trained teachers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I have heard some feedback from NIE trainee teachers in taking Tamil that the curriculum needs review, whether the Ministry will consider teaching training curriculum review in a bid to make the teaching of 	Mother Tongue more accessible?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, basically the school-based provisions, the school-based programmes mean that every school will cater up to 10% of their school cohort who can benefit from greater stretch and challenge, and the schools, all schools will have some teachers who are trained to manage the cognitive as well as the effective requirements of supporting these students who are more inquisitive, who can be challenged further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Then the centre-based advanced modules are those who have either single or multiple domain strengths and opt to go for these modules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The teachers will be pooled from different schools, including some former GEP teachers, centrally held in MOE HQ, and then deployed to teach at various centres.

sections.label: Higher Mother Tongue in secondary school
sections.summary: Higher MTLs in secondary school can be taken regardless of PSLE AL score.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: So, there is also higher MTLs in secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: But noting that there might be some who see MTLs as a strength, you can actually take higher MTLs now, regardless of your PSLE AL score.
